title: Midwatch runbook jotter — incident followups and quick todos
content:
Purpose: quick midwatch scratchpad for follow-ups from the 02:18am pager and other small runbook edits I keep meaning to do. Not formal — just enough to hand off in morning.

TL;DR: brief outage due to cache eviction cascade on prod-kv-01; mitigated by rolling restart of cache-tier and temporary route to warm-cache pool. Root cause likely workload pattern (long prefix churn). Follow-ups + runbook TODOs below.

Incident notes (timeline):
- 02:12 AM: Pager from /alerts/prefix-kv-error — elevated 5xx from inference-router (p50 latency spiked).
- 02:14 AM: SSH to router-2, observed connection retries to cache nodes, error: "kv-miss-queue-overrun" in logs.
- 02:18 AM: Mitigation - set routing policy to prefer warm-cache pool (route: /policy/eviction-throttle -> warm-cache), restarted cache nodes one-at-a-time (cache-01 -> cache-02).
- 02:35 AM: Error rate returned to baseline, latency p95 back within SLO.
- 02:40 AM: Left note in #sre-pager: brief postmortem stub + assigned JIRA-9876.

Immediate followups for morning:
- Add eviction-throttle toggle to emergency runbook (low friction toggle in console with rollback steps). Currently it's only an infra config in a private repo.
- Confirm warm-cache pool autoscale behavior under prefix churn (load test with synthetic prefixes). Tag: @Mina to run 1h test.
- Query logs to find which model/route caused most prefix churn between 01:45-02:15. Searching for high KV churn keys: "user-history-*" looks suspicious.
- Expand alerting to include "kv-miss-queue-overrun" before router errors escalate (reduce alert noise threshold).

Runbook edits (make these quick changes, leave as PR to ops-docs):
- Section: "Cache emergency procedures" — add step: (1) set routing policy to warm-cache; (2) scale cache pool to +2 workers; (3) open ticket in incident-tracker; (4) if errors persist, restart cache nodes sequentially and monitor KV queue depth.
- Add command snippets:
  - Curl policy toggle: curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/policy/eviction-throttle -d '{"state":"on","reason":"pager 02:12"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
  - Check KV queue depth: kubectl -n cache-system exec -it cache-01 -- /bin/sh -c 'redis-cli LLEN kv-queue'
- Include example logs to grep: "kv-miss-queue-overrun" and "prefix-eviction"

Open TODOs (own or hand off):
- [ ] PR to ops-docs with runbook changes (assign to me, ETA EOD).
- [ ] Add synthetic load test harness for prefix churn patterns (Mina).
- [ ] Follow-up with infra on kernel-level OOM handling for cache processes (Ethan).
- [ ] Add unit test for router fallback path to warm-cache (owner: platform-eng).

Notes to self / quick links:
- Pager thread: slack thread #sre-pager (link pinned) — summarize for postmortem later.
- JIRA-9876 created as "Cache eviction cascade — priority P2". Attach logs + timeline.
- Confluence runbook location: confluence://runbooks/cache-emergency (update there).

Small observations / heuristics:
- Pattern: bursty user-history prefixes (seq length variance) often cause kv cache churn when model uses long-term session state. Consider per-prefix TTL or soft-LRU that favors long-lived keys.
- Batching helped on router side but didn't prevent KV queue growth; looks like eviction policy mismatch.

Sticky commands I typed during triage (paste these into runbook snippets):
- kubectl logs -n router inference-router-2 --since=20m | grep "kv-miss"
- redis-cli -h cache-01 info | grep used_memory_human
- curl -s https://metrics/api/series?query=kv_queue_depth | jq '.data'

Questions for morning triage (callout):
- Is warm-cache pool using same VM family as regular cache nodes? If not, cost/latency tradeoffs to be documented.
- How often do we rotate/compact cache keys currently? Is compaction running monthly?

Hand-off blurb for morning SRE:
Ida (night) — noticed transient kv eviction cascade at ~02:12; mitigated by toggling routing policy to warm-cache and sequential restarts. JIRA-9876 has timeline + logs. PR to runbook needed (I will draft). Please escalate to infra if kernel OOM observed in cache nodes or if queue depth remains > 100 for > 5m.

Random micro-tasks (personal):
- reorder my runbook PR checklist (put CLI snippets first).
- move the synthetic-load scripts from my laptop to infra repo.

End of midwatch jotter.

---
Recent pages (compact log):
- 02:12 pager: /alerts/prefix-kv-error -> assigned Ida -> mitigation route set by 02:18 -> resolved 02:35.
- Followups assigned: JIRA-9876 (Ida), load test (Mina), infra kernel follow-up (Ethan).

If I wake up at 06:30 I'll: verify JIRA attachments, open PR draft, ping Mina for test schedule.
